settings.title: Why raw seafood is nature’s perfect pet food

settings.editor: Real seafood, prepared raw and snap-frozen to lock in nutrition. Here’s why more Australian pet owners are making the switch.

settings.title: Fresh, simple food the way pets are built to eat

settings.editor:
Dogs and cats evolved eating fresh, unprocessed prey — not dry pellets cooked at high heat. Raw feeding brings their bowl closer to that natural diet, with real protein and nothing they don’t need.

We chose seafood because it’s one of nature’s richest sources of omega-3s, lean protein and minerals, and because pets simply love the taste. Every meal starts with real Australian seafood, prepared raw and snap-frozen so the goodness stays in.

settings.editor: Seafood packs a lot of goodness into a small, easy-to-digest meal.
Oily fish like salmon is naturally rich in omega-3 fatty acids, which support skin, coat, joints and brain health.
Easy-to-digest protein helps maintain strong muscles and steady energy for active dogs and curious cats.
Salmon belly fins provide calcium and vitamin D to help support healthy bones and teeth.
The fresh smell and taste of seafood wins over even fussy eaters — a big help for picky cats.
No fillers, grains or artificial preservatives. Just seafood, frozen fast to keep it fresh.
Raw food holds its natural moisture, which helps keep pets — especially cats — well hydrated.
Every pet is different, but these are the changes owners most often tell us about after switching to raw seafood.
Omega-3s help nourish skin and give coats a natural shine.
Simple, single-protein meals without fillers are gentle on digestion.
Quality protein supports lean muscle and an active, playful pet.
Pets love the taste, so mealtimes become something to look forward to.
Results vary between pets. If your pet has a health condition, check with your vet before changing their diet.

settings.editor: Yes — when it’s sourced, handled and stored properly. Our seafood is prepared hygienically and snap-frozen to lock in freshness. Keep it frozen until needed, thaw it in the fridge, and wash bowls and hands after serving, just as you would with any raw protein. If your pet has a health condition, check with your vet before changing their diet. Why real seafood works for pets →
Yes. Seafood is a natural, highly palatable protein for both dogs and cats. Start with small portions and follow our feeding guide for how much to serve.
No — it’s made to be served raw. Thaw a portion in the fridge and serve it fridge-cool. Never cook it or microwave it, as heat changes the texture and the natural nutrients we work to protect.

Both work. Many owners start by adding it as a topper to their pet’s usual food, then build up from there. If you’d like raw seafood to be the main diet, talk to your vet about keeping meals complete and balanced for your pet.

Go gradually over about 7–10 days. Start by swapping a small part of their usual meal for raw seafood, then increase the share each day while keeping an eye on their digestion. Puppies, kittens and pets with health conditions should switch under your vet’s guidance. What “natural” pet food really means →
